input.rationale: Section 13.5 gives Corio ownership of Developments it creates, but flips ownership entirely to Commerce One whenever Commerce One supports a Development on an ongoing basis, with no licence back to Corio; the closing sentence likewise leaves ownership of enhancements developed solely by Corio or jointly to future negotiation. Commerce One's retention of its own pre-existing materials and the Software (2.8) is acceptable, and its assignment of Developments is already in place, but for the Commerce One-owned category Corio holds no rights at all, so the clause fails the fallback (broad licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables). We therefore add the fallback licence-back and, since no clause addresses our data, the required limit on any Commerce One licence in Corio/Customer data.

proposal.summary: Add licence-back for Commerce One-owned Developments and limit any Commerce One licence in Corio data.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 13.5 lets Commerce One take ownership of coding Corio creates (and leaves Corio-developed enhancements to later negotiation) with no licence back, so we have added our fallback position: a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense those Developments for our business, plus a limit confining any Commerce One licence in our data to processing it solely to provide the services.

ops.text: To the extent Commerce One owns or retains ownership of any Developments, enhancements, modifications or derivative works developed by Corio under this Section 13, Commerce One grants Corio a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense the same for Corio's business. Any license granted to Commerce One in data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Corio or its Customers is limited to processing that data solely to provide the services under this Agreement.
